messages:
maria: Heads-up — ran a 48h perf run against allocator+kv changes on p40-32gb. Hit multiple OOMs during KV prefill-heavy workloads. Dumped a short summary below.

ben: can you paste the alloc/frag summary + kernel routing logs?

maria: sure, excerpt:
```
KV cache peak: 29.7GB
Workspace allocated: 32.0GB
Observed fragmentation (free but unusable): 3.2GB
Largest slab-waste (per-slab avg): 1.8GB
Prefill-triggered evictions: 14% of requests -> eviction storms at 80% util
Kernel fallback events: 1.2k (int8 fallback triggered due to workspace pressure)
```

carol: ouch. were per-request caps enabled on that run? last time prefill+decode contention made it worse.

maria: we had per-request cap=1g (hard). That allowed prefill to grab big contiguous slabs, but many small decode allocations caused fragmentation. Proposed mitigations:
```
- introduce "memory-stitching" evictor that coalesces adjacent free slabs before re-allocating
- soft prefill cap = 384MB per request (soft, yields under pressure)
- decode hardcap = 768MB per request
- prefill concurrency throttle: max 6 concurrent prefill tasks per worker
```

danny: any sim numbers for the coalescing approach?

maria: sim results (48h synthetic trace) vs current:
```
- fragmentation down 42% (3.2GB -> ~1.85GB)
- KV eviction churn down 37%
- no-OOM in 48h synthetic window (previously 3 OOMs)
- tail (p99) token latency improved 12% under 90% util
- extra alloc bookkeeping added ~1.5ms median to allocation path when coalescing triggered; p99 alloc_cost ~1.8ms
```

ben: the extra alloc path cost worries me for short-seq low-latency traffic. Can we make coalesce opt-in behind a flag and only trigger when free-frag > X?

maria: yep. plan is: coalesce only when fragmentation ratio > 0.15 or workspace headroom < 1.2GB. Fallback to thin-slab allocator for short sequences.

perf-bot: perf-bot: quick metrics probe: alloc_coalesce_time p50=0.12ms p95=0.9ms p99=1.8ms; prefill_concurrency p95=5.8

carol: also consider prefilling only top-k KV entries for large requests (hybrid prefill/decode). reduces prefill size and preserves hit-rate.

maria: good call  will prototype top-k prefill heuristic (k=128 default). Reproducer for canary:
```
./tools/kv-stress --trace synthetic/large-prefill.json --prefill-rate 0.6 --req-cap 800 --topk-prefill 128
```

ben: SGTM. i'll own canary rollout and add safety gates: 24h no-OOM, p99 token latency not regressed >5%.

danny: add an integration test asserting no OOMs across 1M-sample window and a frag regression alert.

maria: opening PR with flags, perf harness, and rollout plan. tagging @ben for canary. Thanks :party-parrot:
